input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS 140-3 remediation of KServe serving-stack images

## Description

This epic makes every KServe-component serving image run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated
crypto in the request path. It covers auditing the KServe component images and the
serving data plane within the KServe component scope for non-validated
cryptographic library usage, remediating those usages against validated modules,
and verifying the remediated images on a FIPS-enabled cluster.

## Scope

- Audit all serving-stack images owned by the KServe component and produce a
  module inventory listing the cryptographic modules linked into each image and
  flagging every non-validated crypto usage in the request path.
- Replace or rebuild each non-validated crypto usage in the request path against
  FIPS-validated cryptographic modules.
- Rebuild the affected images through the existing build pipeline.
- Run functional verification of the inference request path (InferenceService
  deployment and serving) on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster and record the test
  results.
- Hand off the module inventory and the verification test results as inputs to the
  compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory exists covering every KServe-component serving image in the
  stack, listing linked cryptographic modules and flagging each non-validated
  usage in the request path.
- An image scan of every remediated image shows no non-validated cryptographic
  module linked in the request path.
- Remediated images build successfully through the existing serving-stack build
  pipeline.
- Functional verification on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster passes for the
  inference request path, and the test results are recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path).
  This epic delivers the KServe-component portion, including the serving data
  plane within the KServe component scope.

# FIPS regression gating check for KServe serving-stack builds

## Description

This epic adds a gating CI check to the KServe serving-stack build pipeline that
fails any build whose image reintroduces non-validated crypto usage in the request
path, so FIPS regressions are caught before shipping rather than rediscovered at
the next audit.

## Scope

- Implement a detection check that scans built serving-stack images for
  non-validated cryptographic module usage in the request path, using the same
  validated-module criteria as the remediation audit.
- Wire the check into the KServe serving-stack build pipeline as a gating step
  (a failed check blocks the build from shipping; it is not advisory).
- Validate the check with both test polarities: a deliberately non-compliant
  build fails, and a compliant build passes. The compliant test image may be
  constructed locally for the test (for example, rebuilt against validated
  crypto modules) — it does not need to come from the FIPS remediation work,
  so this validation does not sequence this epic on that remediation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gating check runs on every KServe serving-stack build in the pipeline.
- A build whose image reintroduces non-validated crypto usage in the request path
  fails the check, demonstrated with a deliberately non-compliant test build.
- The check is gating: a failed check blocks the build from shipping.
- A build whose image contains only validated crypto in the request path passes
  the check.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** — CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. This epic
  delivers the KServe-builds portion.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model
serving stack — module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and
submits it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Assemble the module inventory covering every serving-stack image in scope (KServe
  component images and the Platform Operator image), consolidated from the
  remediation outcomes.
- Collect the signed build attestations produced by the serving-stack build
  pipelines for the remediated images.
- Collect the FIPS verification test results from the remediated images.
- Assemble the evidence package to the security review board's submission
  requirements for the defined certification milestones.
- Submit the package through the security review board to the external
  certification lab and confirm the submission.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package includes a module inventory covering every serving-stack
  image in scope.
- The evidence package includes the signed build attestations produced by the
  serving-stack build pipelines for the remediated images.
- The evidence package includes the FIPS verification test results from the
  remediated images.
- The evidence package is submitted through the security review board to the
  external certification lab, and the submission is confirmed.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification lab turnaround is historically six to nine months and the
  review-board cadence is externally controlled; neither can be compressed by
  engineering effort. These are schedule risks on this epic, not acceptance
  conditions — the acceptance criteria above are written at the
  engineering-controlled endpoint (assembly and confirmed submission).
- Security review board sign-off at the defined milestones is a mandatory human
  process gate embedded in the submission route.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab. This epic delivers it in full.

# FIPS support posture documentation for the model serving stack

## Description

This epic documents the FIPS 140-3 support posture of the model serving stack and
the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters,
published through the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

Content outline (authored and published through the docs content process):

- FIPS support posture of the serving stack: which images run with validated
  cryptographic modules on FIPS-enabled clusters, and what "no non-validated crypto
  in the request path" means for the deployed stack.
- Cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster requirements and any
  configuration needed to run the serving stack in FIPS mode.
- Scope boundary: the FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training is
  covered by separate strategies and is explicitly out of scope here, as is Common
  Criteria certification.
- How the CI gating check protects the posture (what a failed FIPS regression
  check means for a build).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture for the model serving
  stack.
- Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for running the serving
  stack on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented FIPS posture and
  passes that review.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites. This epic delivers it in full.

compliance evidence process, documentation), with mandatory external process gates.
